body: Privilege escalation: `canManage()` returns true when the caller has only the `view` scope on all groups. So a view-only admin passes `requireManage()` and can, for example, create top-level groups via `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`. This check should require `MANAGE` only, the same as `canManage(GroupModel)`. The javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator#canManage()`, which mentions VIEW, needs the same fix.

`getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` looks broken. `findByType(server, "Groups")` only returns the all-groups type resource: per-group resources come from `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`, which calls `resourceStore.create(server, name, owner)` and never sets a type. That means per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` grants are never found here. Two more problems follow. First, `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` passes the resource's UUID, but `hasPermission` resolves resources with `findByName`, and resources are named by group id, so the lookup always falls back to the type resource. Second, `granted.add(groupResource.getId())` adds the authz resource id rather than a group id. If an all-groups view-members permission exists, `UserModel.GROUPS` gets set to `{<Groups resource UUID>}`, the user search filters on a group that doesn't exist, and it returns no users. `grantIfNoPermission(true)` has also been turned on at that point. Compare `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission`, which uses `resource.getName()`.
Javadoc copy/paste mistake: `requireManageMembers` delegates to `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, not `canManageMembership(GroupModel)`.
